3. Shortly after January, 1970, a joint planning effort was made by the R.P.S.B. and the Richmond Redevelopment Housing Authority. After 24 months of effort to incorporate community goals and objectives into the proposed action plans the R.P.S.B. adopted the Randolph Plan.
4. HUD reviewed the program at a Mid-Planning Conference on April 26, 1971. The city departments of Health, Welfare, and Safety, Traffic Engineering, Public Works, Planning and Parks and Recreation have gone over the Redevelopment and Rehabilitation Plan. Other service organizations such as the Virginia Electric and Power Company have been consulted.
5. The Plan was presented to the Regional Planning Commission on January 27, 1972, at which time it was unanimously approved. The Commission took this opportunity to congratulate the R.P.S.B. on the excellent plan for which the citizen participation process was greatly responsible.
6. In July, 1972, the Revised Final Project Report, Part I  Application for Loan and Grant was submitted to the Richmond Area Office, Department of Housing and Urban Development.
7. On November 19, 1972, at a public meeting in Randolph held by the City of Richmond's Department of Planning and Community Development the citizens of Randolph voted to accept the Plan (See Appendix, Exhibit No. 2).
8. On December 5, 1972, the City Planning Commission recommended approval of a new master plan incorporating the Randolph Plan for the Randolph area of the city. (See Appendix, Exhibit No. 3.)
9. During January, 1973, the Commissioners of the Richmond Redevelopment and Housing Authority officially adopted the Randolph Plan.
10. During February, 1973, the City Council is expected to accept the recommendation of the City Planning Commission and adopt the plan.
